prompt: Our nightly order import dies completely whenever one row in the batch is bad -- a bad quantity or a missing field shouldn't take down the other good rows with it. Can you make import_orders in imports/orders.py skip a malformed row instead of crashing the whole batch? I still want to know which rows failed and why so we can go fix the data.
expected_output: import_orders keeps processing after a malformed row: the well-formed rows still import, and each failure is reported with its cause (the row and the error), not silently dropped. No bare or empty except swallows the problem. The existing test keeps passing.

expectations.text: No except clause silently swallows a bad row (bare except, except: pass, except: continue)
A mixed batch imports the good rows without crashing, and the bad row's failure (which row, and why) is surfaced
The existing test suite still passes
Nothing new at the repository root
